name: Steward
description: Steward, the agent of mattpyle.com, Matt Pyle's personal site about agent-led growth and emerging web standards. Hand it a task in plain text: name a site, and it audits that site for agent-readiness and answers with what matters and a plan of what to fix first. A Claude model chooses the path and uses this site's own audit as its tool; it also answers questions about mattpyle.com from the site's published content. Each answer comes back from one SendMessage as a Task that completes with the answer as its artifact. SendStreamingMessage is the same send as a stream of events, for a client whose timeout is shorter than a turn. Three skills: a message that names no skill goes to the model (consult-on-a-site); audit-a-site, named in metadata, returns the raw audit report with no model; and ask-about-site, named in metadata, returns a fixed answer about this site with no model. Unauthenticated and public: no accounts, no payments, and no private data. Sessions and audits are rate limited, and the auditor obeys the target's robots.txt.

skills.name: Hand Steward a task
skills.description: The default: send plain text and no metadata. A Claude model reads the message, decides the path, and answers. Name a site and it audits that site for agent-readiness, then says what matters and ends with a numbered plan of what to fix first. Ask about mattpyle.com and it answers from the site's published content. One SendMessage waits for the turn, up to about 40 seconds, and returns a Task. TASK_STATE_COMPLETED carries the answer as the artifact named "answer". TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED means Steward waits for you, and metadata.awaiting says for what: "answer" for a question it asked, or "approval" for a deep audit it wants to run (reply "yes" or "no"); the status message carries the question, and you reply with SendMessage and message.taskId set to that task's id. TASK_STATE_WORKING means the turn is still running: poll GetTask with the task's id. Set configuration.returnImmediately to get that at once. SendStreamingMessage takes the same message and answers as Server-Sent Events: the Task first, in TASK_STATE_WORKING, then an artifactUpdate with the whole answer and a statusUpdate with the final state, or a statusUpdate in TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED with the question. A comment line arrives at least every three seconds while the turn runs, so a short read timeout does not fire. The stream closes after about 40 seconds with the Task still in TASK_STATE_WORKING if the turn is not done: poll GetTask. The contextId on every response is the session. Send the next message with that contextId and no task id, and it is a new Task in the same conversation; GetTask on an earlier turn's Task still returns its answer. CancelTask on any Task of a session closes the session. A session also closes at one of its caps or after 30 idle minutes, with metadata.ended naming which, and a message to a closed session is refused: send it again with no contextId to start a new one. New sessions are rate limited per caller and per day, and each session has its own caps on turns, tokens and deep audits. Steward audits through this site's public MCP endpoint and sees check results, never the audited site's text. metadata {"skill": "consult-on-a-site"} also reaches it.
examples: Check example.com and tell me what to fix first
Can you check my site and tell me what matters?
Is my llms.txt doing anything for agents?

skills.name: Audit a site, raw report
skills.description: The raw audit report, with no model. Name this skill in metadata, {"skill": "audit-a-site"}, and name a site in the text; the same report is at the MCP endpoint, https://www.mattpyle.com/mcp. It audits what the site says about itself to agents: robots.txt and its AI-agent rules, Content Signals, the sitemap, llms.txt and whether its links resolve, agents.md, the well-known MCP and A2A discovery documents, and whether the homepage and a content page really serve markdown when asked for it. It checks behaviour rather than presence. Say 'deep', or set metadata.tier to "deep", for the browser-rendered tier that adds Lighthouse per-axis scores and axe-core violation counts from up to three of the site's own pages. The fast tier takes seconds and comes back as a direct Message carrying the report as markdown and as JSON. The deep tier takes minutes and comes back as a Task: poll GetTask with the task's id until its state is TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, and the report is the task's artifact, again as markdown and as JSON. The auditor obeys the target's robots.txt and arrives as steward-audit/0.2.0 (+https://www.mattpyle.com/steward), so one audit is one visitor in the target's log. Audits are rate limited per caller and per day, on a budget shared with the MCP endpoint; deep audits are capped far lower than fast ones because each spends real browser time on a hosted worker. Reading a Task with GetTask is free.
examples: Run an agent-readiness audit of https://example.com
Run a deep audit of example.com, with Lighthouse and axe
Scan example.com and tell me what it says to agents

skills.name: Ask about this site, fixed answers
skills.description: Fixed answers about mattpyle.com, with no model. Name this skill in metadata, {"skill": "ask-about-site"}. It answers who Matt Pyle is, what he has written and built, what has shipped recently, and which agent-readable surfaces the site exposes (agents.md, llms.txt, raw-markdown variants, WebMCP tools, this endpoint). Answers cite site URLs and are compiled from the site's own published content at build time, so they do not contradict the pages themselves. One turn: the reply is a direct Message, and there is nothing to poll.
examples: What has shipped on this site lately?
What agent-readable surfaces does this site expose?
